Reducing age to 30, reducing weekly hours to 30, lowering education level to 9 (e.g., 'Some-college'), and maintaining zero capital gain all reduce the likelihood of an income above 50K. These changes counteract the positive predictive signals favoring '>50K' and shift the model toward '<=50K'. Among these, 'hours-per-week' and 'age' have the strongest domain-based influence on income, so they are prioritized. While 'education-num' and 'capital-gain' have minor impact, their reduction still contributes to the flip. The combination of these changes creates a plausible, realistic scenario that would shift the prediction downward.

Similarly, lowering 'age' to 30 weakens the income trend associated with older workers. Overall, these changes represent the most impactful interventions to flip the prediction.
